header.tagline: Show-ready audio playback for theatre, radio, events and parties
header.intro: Line up your music and effects, fire each one at the right moment, and keep going when something goes wrong. Free for Windows, macOS and Linux, LivePlay suits a party playlist as well as a full theatre or radio show.
header.screenshotAlt: LivePlay main window with the playlist, cart player and mixer side by side

download.title: Download LivePlay
download.subtitle: Free and open-source. Available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

macGatekeeper.title: macOS: "LivePlay is damaged and can't be opened"?
macGatekeeper.intro: LivePlay is not yet signed with an Apple Developer certificate, so macOS quarantines it on download. The app is safe — this just means Apple hasn't been paid to notarize it. To open it, remove the quarantine flag once after installing to /Applications:
macGatekeeper.outro: Enter your password when prompted, then launch LivePlay normally. You only need to do this once per install.

winSmartScreen.title: Windows: "Windows protected your PC"?
winSmartScreen.intro: LivePlay isn't yet signed with a certificate Microsoft SmartScreen recognises, so Windows may show a blue "Windows protected your PC" warning when you run the installer. The app is safe — it simply hasn't built up download reputation yet (code signing is on the way).
winSmartScreen.step1: Click "More info" on the warning dialog.
winSmartScreen.step2: Click the "Run anyway" button that appears, then continue the installation normally.
winSmartScreen.outro: If your browser blocked the download instead, choose "Keep" to save the installer first.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.subtitle: LivePlay is free and open-source — and always will be.
contribute.freeText: LivePlay is completely free to download and use — no licence fees, no subscriptions, no paywalls. Every feature is available to everyone, with no premium tiers.
contribute.licenseText: LivePlay is released under the GNU AGPL-3.0 licence. In plain terms: you are free to use, study, share and modify it. If you share a modified version — or run it as a network service — you must make your source code available under the same licence, so the whole community keeps benefiting.
contribute.contributeText: Anyone can contribute. Report bugs, suggest features, improve translations or submit code — every contribution is welcome. Head to the GitHub repository to open an issue or a pull request.

groupShow.title: Run your show
groupShow.intro: Everything you need to put a show together and run it with confidence.

playlist.title: Cue It Up, Fire It Off
playlist.description: Drag your music and effects into a playlist of cues, and choose how each one leads into the next: play on, loop or jump. Control the whole running order from your mouse, touchscreen, keyboard or MIDI controller.

cart.title: Instant Sounds and Jingles
cart.description: Keep jingles, stings and announcements a single tap away in the cart player, ready to fire over whatever else is playing.

ducking.title: Automatic Ducking
ducking.description: Let announcements and effects dip the music while they play and bring it back smoothly afterwards, or have a cue clear everything else for a clean change of scene.

interface.title: Organised Your Way
interface.description: Group cues by scene, act or set, colour-code them, and reorder them whenever the running order changes. Arrange the playlist, cart player and mixer to suit you, tuck away what you don't need, and in the desktop app move the cart player or mixer to a second screen.

showMode.title: Show Mode
showMode.description: Show Mode turns the screen into large, touch-friendly controls and hides everything that could edit the show, so nothing gets changed by accident once the doors open.

waveform.title: Waveform Trimmer
waveform.description: Trim every sound to exactly the part you want and shape its fades right on the waveform. LivePlay can also trim silence and even out levels for you, so every cue arrives at a consistent volume.

properties.title: Fine-Tune Every Cue
properties.description: Name and colour each cue, set its level, choose where it plays, and decide what happens when it starts and ends, all in one place.

youtube.title: YouTube Integration
youtube.description: Pull audio straight from YouTube into your show when you need a track in a hurry. Please make sure you have the rights to use what you download.

firstLaunch.title: Quick Setup
firstLaunch.description: Pick a folder, name your show and start adding sounds. LivePlay keeps your media together with the project, so moving a show to another computer is simple.

groupMixer.title: Mix it properly
groupMixer.intro: A built-in mixer, so music, effects and voices each sit right in the room and nothing unexpected reaches the speakers.

mixer.title: A Real Mixer for Your Show
mixer.description: Give music, effects and announcements their own buses and balance them on channel strips, just as you would on a desk. Route buses into each other, straight to an output or through aux sends, and assign a whole group of cues in one go.

eqDynamics.title: EQ and Dynamics on Every Bus
eqDynamics.description: Shape every bus with a parametric EQ and a live spectrum analyser, then keep it under control with a gate and a compressor. Stereo buses can be widened or narrowed, with the low end kept solid in the centre.

limiter.title: Brick-Wall Limiter & Loudness Targets
limiter.description: A brick-wall limiter on every output keeps stray peaks away from the speakers, and the mixer shows you whenever it is working. Pick a loudness target, from broadcast and streaming to live, and the limiter, meters and waveforms all follow it.

meters.title: Broadcast-Grade Metering
meters.description: Accurate real-time meters on every cue, bus and output, in the scale you work in. Their colour zones follow your loudness target, so you can see at a glance whether you are in spec.

preview.title: Headphone Preview and PFL
preview.description: Listen to the next cue, or to any bus, in your headphones without the audience hearing a thing, and check how a mix holds up in mono before it goes out.

routing.title: Hardware Outputs That Travel With You
routing.description: Your show talks to outputs by name, such as Main, Foyer or Sub, and each computer links those names to its own sound cards, several at once if you need them. Take the show to a new venue and LivePlay points out anything missing, so you can remap it in moments.

fades.title: Fades, Loops and Timing
fades.description: Give every cue its own fades, loop ambiences without a seam, and choose whether the next cue crossfades, waits or starts on a marker. Groups show how long they run and how much time is left.

groupSystem.title: Built to be relied on
groupSystem.intro: From a single laptop to a networked system run by a whole team, LivePlay is designed to keep the show going.

remoteOperation.title: Local or Remote Operation
remoteOperation.description: Run the audio engine on the same computer or on a machine backstage with your audio interfaces, and control everything from anywhere on the network. The sound comes from the engine, not the screen, so the show keeps playing even if a control computer drops out.

discovery.title: Work Together, Recover Quickly
discovery.description: Screens find LivePlay on the network by themselves, and several people can work on the same show at once, all seeing the same cues. If a connection drops it comes back on its own, and if the engine ever stops it restarts and picks the show back up.

accounts.title: Accounts, Roles and API Tokens
accounts.description: Give your team their own sign-ins, with operators running the show and administrators looking after the system. Show-control tools such as Companion get their own access tokens, and you can move your whole team to another LivePlay server in one go.

settingsPage.title: All Your Settings in One Place
settingsPage.description: All your settings live on one page. Personal preferences such as language and theme follow you to any screen you sign in on, while the show itself sounds the same everywhere.

audioEngine.title: Robust C++ Audio Engine
audioEngine.description: At the heart of LivePlay is a dedicated audio engine that talks directly to your sound hardware on Windows, macOS and Linux. Every cue plays independently, so the same sound can be fired twice at different levels and always behaves as you expect.

ltc.title: SMPTE Timecode
ltc.description: Send SMPTE timecode with your cues, so lighting, video and other equipment can follow your show.

ports.title: Network Ports
ports.subtitle: If you're running the server and client on different machines, make sure these ports are open on your network and firewall.

control.title: Control Connection
control.description: REST API and WebSocket connection carrying transport commands, project data, routing and live meters between the client and server.

discovery.title: Automatic Discovery
discovery.description: Broadcast and multicast beacon (group 239.255.69.80) that lets clients find LivePlay servers on the local network automatically.

ports.note: A single-machine install needs no configuration — the client and server talk over 127.0.0.1 and the Windows installer adds the firewall rules for you. These ports only matter when separating the control position from the audio hardware across a LAN.

api.title: API & Automation
api.subtitle: Connect LivePlay to your show-control tools.
api.description: Control playback, edit projects and routing, and monitor live state over HTTP and WebSocket. When login is on, give Companion, a show-control system or a script its own API token from Settings, under Accounts, instead of sharing someone's password. The developer reference covers authentication, every endpoint, commands, events and integration examples.
